title: Chapter 69 — Account Growth Planning
intro: The annual growth plan per account — targets, strategies, and quarterly checkpoints.

sections.title: The Annual Account Plan
sections.content:
Every Tier 1 and Tier 2 trade account deserves a written annual plan. Not a novel — one page. Last year's revenue. This year's target. The specific growth strategy: category expansion, share consolidation, new project types, or geographic expansion.

Review the plan with the account at the start of the year: 'Last year we did $85K together across 12 projects. I believe we can hit $110K this year if we add the laundry category to your specs. Here is how I see that working.' The builder who sees a growth plan knows you are treating their business as a strategic partnership, not a transactional relationship.

sections.title: Quarterly Checkpoints
sections.content:
Review progress quarterly. Pull the numbers. Are we tracking to the annual target? If ahead — why? How do we sustain it? If behind — why? What changed? What do we need to adjust?

The quarterly checkpoint is where you catch problems early. A builder who is at 20 percent of their annual volume through Q2 is either having a slow year or splitting volume with a competitor. The conversation tells you which — and what to do about it.

sections.title: The Growth Conversation
sections.content:
Growth conversations should feel collaborative, not pressuring. 'I noticed your laundry is still going through [competitor]. What would it take for us to earn that category? Is it pricing, availability, or something else?'

Often the answer is simple — they never thought to ask, or your competitor had a relationship from before you started working together. Sometimes the answer reveals a real gap you need to close. Either way, you cannot grow what you do not discuss.
